newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's T-bill yield to be at market level.
newsitem.headline: Russia's T-bill yield to be at market level.

text.p: The yield at a Wednesday's auction of 182-day GKO discount Treasury bills will be in line with market levels on healthy demand and banks will not bid aggressively, dealers said on Tuesday.
The average price at an auction of OFZ interest-bearing bonds will depend on the results of the T-bills auction, they said.
TOMORROW
Finance Ministry sells:
*4.00 trln rbls 714-day new bond tranche (series 24012)
*7.50 trln rbls 182-day T-bills (series 22083)
Finance Ministry repays:
*7.18 trln rbls maturing 224-day T-bills (series 22052)
TODAY
*Average yield fell to 28.05 pct from 28.57 pct on Monday
*Turnover rose to 4.75 trln rbls from 3.84 trln rbls
*Central Bank sold 100.77 bln rbls of series 23006 and 24012 bills

Dealers forecast the average yield on the series 22083 T-bill, maturing on November 12, 1997, would be in the 28.02-28.74 percent range. The series 22070 bills, maturing on November 19, 1997, closed on Tuesday at 87.19 percent to yield 28.22 percent.
The average price on an additional tranche of series 24012 bonds, maturing on April 28, 1999, would be in the 98.14-98.37 percent range. The original issue closed at 98.20 to yield 36.64 percent.
CS First Boston head of forex department Sergei Koshelenko said the yield at the T-bill auction would be in line with the market.
"When overnight money is so cheap, nothing bad can happen to the T-bill," he said.
On Tuesday overnight credit rouble/dollar rate was 5-15 percent after 5-10 percent on Monday.
Dealers said they did not expect a premium over market yields at the T-bill auction as the volume of foreign funds flowingout due to maturity payments would be compensated by an inflow of new funds.
Dealers forecast the OFZ bond price would be at market levels.
--Anna Smirnova, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
